messages.subject: Setting basis size (k) in dsm
parts:
Hello List!

I'm running some dsm models to assess which covariables influence guanaco distribution. When using s(x,y) or s(x) and checking the basis size, I get a low p-value. I tried doubling the k to see what happens but I keep getting the same problem. 
I read at https://github.com/DistanceDevelopment/spatial-workshops/blob/master/slides/dsm3-model-checking.pdf
that sometimes other things can cause a low p-value and k isn't the problem, but the slides do not provide much information about the other reasons.  

I wanted to ask what other reasons could these be? What else can I try to make the model fit better?

Thank you very much in advance, 
Regards, 

Antonella

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Setting basis size (k) in dsm
parts:
Hi Antonella, hi listfolk,

It's likely the case that this covariate "doesn't matter" in the model,
so there's nothing that you can really do to "make" it significant (and
in fact this is not a good idea in general).

"Doesn't matter" probably deserves some unpacking here -- likely it's
the case that there is simply not enough signal in the data for the
covariate to explain any of the variation. This can happen if (for your
example, presumably geographical coordinates) there isn't any variation
in, say, Easting. In some cases one might be better off estimating
abundance or density using design-based methods (Horvitz-Thompson
estimation).

Hope this helps,
--dave


PS. with apologies for the delay in my reply here.
